definition: A property of matter that is either positive or negative: like charges repel and unlike charges attract.
A tiny negatively charged particle found around the nucleus of every atom; in metals some electrons are free to move.
A material that lets electric charge flow through it easily, such as a metal, because it has free electrons.
A material, such as plastic or rubber, that does not let electric charge flow through it because its electrons are held tightly in their atoms.
The unit of electric charge, symbol C: the charge that passes a point when a current of 1 A flows for 1 s.
A region where an electric charge experiences a force; its direction at a point is the way a positive charge there would be pushed.
